result.summary: AU-R3 fixes KRITIK-R finding L2. The change is in scripts/audio/modern/audio_feed.gd; no sound file, level or music was touched. `_paving()` no longer puts old-town cobbles on a bridge without a stone deck. A concrete deck in a city is asphalt again: the Venice causeway had cobbles on 211 of its 378 m, now on none. Steel decks stay "deck", stone bridges stay cobbled, and the joints per deck are unchanged. `cobbled_blocks()` now shares out the cobbles over street metres only. The bridges without a stone deck are taken out of the base through `bridge_stretches`, which reads them from the plan, so every arrival in a city gets the same blocks. Where such a bridge cuts an old town and the share then misses 0.6 ± 0.05, single moves bring it back into the band (`COBBLE_BAND`). Measured over all 64 stages in both directions, with both feeds driven in 1-m steps: there are 34 non-stone bridges in 30 old towns; 16 of them had cobbles before and none has now. 18 old towns sound different, all of them with such a bridge, and every other town is bit-identical. Every old town with such a bridge is inside the band except Lyon, which is pushed out by its stone bridge. Kiel–Hamburg is unchanged: 0 of 9,500 feed states differ and the autopilot trigger log is identical, so the AU-R previews stay valid. The new tests fail on the old code and pass now. Gates: run_tests 656 tests with 0 failures, golden 20 of 20 identical, arcade_lean OK, 0 changed lines in the frozen paths. Still open, reported but not changed (it predates this round): 9 of the 16 old towns with a stone bridge, and two tunnels inside old towns.

notes_for_next: Stone bridges: count their metres as pre-cobbled in cobbled_blocks. This would bring the 16 stone-bridge towns into the band and change their blocks; Hamburg is not affected.
Old towns without a bridge stay at 0.55–0.56 (the greedy undershoots on 800-m centres). Applying COBBLE_BAND to every centre would change Hamburg, and the previews would then need re-recording.

Nobody has listened. The audible change is limited to old towns with concrete bridges, the Venice causeway being the prominent one. A short Venice preview could be recorded if the user wants to hear it.

result.quality_verdict: What changes for the player: in 13 old towns the concrete bridges (16 bridges) no longer sound cobbled. The most noticeable is the Venice causeway, which is now asphalt over its full 378 m with the same 32-m concrete joints, as it is in reality. The streets around these bridges keep or regain about 60 % cobbles (measured 0.57–0.65), and no old town loses cobbles to a bridge. Kiel–Hamburg, the stage of the first test build, is unchanged in every feed decision, so the build and the previews the user has are unaffected. Not yet good: by the street metric, 9 old towns with stone bridges are outside the band (0.46–0.75) because of the AU-R allocation, and Lyon moved from 0.53 to 0.68 because of its stone bridge. These are measured and reported, not fixed, because the brief allowed no other sound change. Nobody has listened to any of this, and no new preview was recorded.

result.verdict: Aus Sicht Code, Auslösung und Regressionen ist der AU-R3-Kopf b6339ad4 für die Testversion abnahmefähig: Es gibt keinen Blocker, alle Gates sind grün (gemessen: run_tests 656 Tests ohne Fehler, golden 20 von 20, check_arcade_lean, Regel-1-Dateien unverändert, ERGEBNIS in drei Bild-/Klang-Modi gleich, beide Generatoren bitgleich). result.verdict: The final Modern sound head b6339ad passes my independent acceptance measurement. I found no blocker and no high finding: one medium (a thin V3 margin for trucks) and three low ones. Keeping the character holds: the layers on their own differ from AU-C1 by at most 0.53 dB per third-octave and 0.22 LU, the game mixes by at most 0.89 dB at 32 Hz (engine scatter). The slab layer follows its law: steady at 150 km/h, −0.82 dB at 170 km/h and −1.96 dB at 200 km/h against AU-R, timbre within 0.57 dB of AU-C1. V1 holds with margin in two new seeds (at most 0.239). V3 holds: crash p95 is 2.05 dB (car) and 2.66 dB (truck), every crash is at or below −1.21 dBTP, and cruising peaks at 0.22 dB. The worst case is −1.54 dBTP. All 28 loops play sample-exact, there is no new tone, no zipper and no pumping, and road CPU is +0.05–0.08 ms per frame against AU-C1 (locks 2/s, only at 110–150 km/h on concrete). I proved that the "nachher" half and the game-mix preview are the current head's sound, two ways: they contain the head's own loop files (correlation 0.41/0.70 against ≤0.12 for other heads), and a fresh recording of the same drive on the head matches them within 0.2 dB above 500 Hz. The named preview marks are within 0.15 s; "Bankett"/"Leitplanke" are 0.6–1.5 s early. Everything is measured on this loaded VM (llvmpipe, Dummy audio driver). Whether anything is audible, how the 0.9-dB single stones or the −3-dB slab dip at 130 km/h sound to a person, and Steam Deck behaviour are inferred only — nobody listened here.

findings.problem: V3 holds for trucks, but only just. The p95 limiter gain reduction over 60 heavy truck crashes is 2.66 dB against a 3-dB limit, and 3 of 60 crashes exceed 3 dB. A p95 taken from 60 random crashes is itself noisy, so a future gate run with new seeds can fail without any change to the sound.

Option (b) is a 0.5-dB mix change to the truck hit and must be re-measured with 60 crashes.

findings.problem: In Godot, realigning a slab pattern is a hard cut. play(pos) on a playing player starts the new playback with no fade-in while the old one fades out over about 470 samples. The quieter design therefore steps by its own sample value at the new position and has an 11-ms double image.
findings.evidence: Godot behaviour, measured with a 441-Hz sine (kr_restart.gd): the step on restart is 0.48 at amplitude 0.49; volume changes ramp over 405 samples; stop() fades over 408 samples. Slab files: the sample at a random position is median −25/−20 dB and in 10 % of cases above −13/−11 dB below the strike peak. result.summary: I fixed all seven findings without changing a sound file or the music, and every gate is green. H1–H4 and M2: I added three tests to test_road_audio.gd and widened two. A stage tunnel moves blocks only when it pushes the share out of 0.6 ± 0.05, and every old town is pulled back into that range. With the reviewer's 1-m drive over all 128 plans, arrivals out of range went from 14 to 3. All 3 measure 0.549 (Barcelona twice, Ljubljana once) but are set to exactly 0.550. Over 60 heavy truck crashes the limiter's 95th-percentile gain reduction went from 2.78/2.72 dB to 2.13/2.51 dB in two seeds, and 2.34 dB over all 120 crashes. True peak max is −1.39 dBTP (measured).
